title: Loch Modan
body: Loch Modan is a highland of green hills and pine woods east of Dun Morogh, named for the great lake at its heart, whose waters the dwarves hold back with the Stonewrought Dam. The orcs overran it in the Second War and the dwarves won it back. Today it is thinly guarded, its soldiers called away to distant fronts, while troggs boil up out of the earth, ogres raid from the northeast and Dark Iron saboteurs creep toward the dam.

title: Valley of Kings
body: Where the road from Dun Morogh comes through the mountains, two colossal stone dwarves stand watch over the pass into the southlands: King Madoran Bronzebeard and King Khardros Wildhammer. Their sons raised them after both kings had died, as a warning to any who would attack the dwarven realms and a reminder of the price the Dark Irons paid for their treachery.

title: Thelsamar
body: Thelsamar is the chief town of Loch Modan, a cluster of stout dwarven houses on the western shore of the loch, on the road between Dun Morogh and the Wetlands. The Explorers' League keeps a branch house here for its digs, and the town is famous for its blood sausages.

title: Dun Algaz
body: Dun Algaz is the mountain pass that carries the road north out of Loch Modan into the Wetlands. Its stronghold has a bloody past: when the Horde was driven south in the Second War, Dun Algaz became its last hold, and the assault Anduin Lothar ordered against it failed. Now the orcs are back, as Dragonmaw warriors from the Wetlands push into the pass.

title: Stonewrought Dam
body: The Stonewrought Dam spans the northern end of the loch, a vast wall of stone holding back its waters, which spill down a great waterfall toward the Wetlands. It is counted among the greatest works the dwarves ever built. Since the Thandol Span fell, its keepers fear the Dark Irons mean it to be next, and with most of its guard called to the front, they have reason.

parts.body: They were right. Dark Iron insurgents swam a keg of seaforium powder to the base of the dam, and it was disarmed only just in time.

title: The Farstrider Lodge
body: In southeastern Loch Modan stands the Farstrider Lodge, a hunting lodge built in the high elven style, though only one elf still lives there. Dwarven and human hunters fill it now, drawn by the loch's famous crocolisks, whose skins and meat always find buyers.

title: Ironband's Excavation Site
body: East of the loch, Prospector Ironband of the Explorers' League digs into ancient ruins, or did until Stonesplinter troggs surfaced within the site and drove the dwarves out. The troggs came up just after the diggers uncovered a large number of strange carved idols, which now lie in trogg hands.

parts.body: The idols have a strange effect on the creatures, says the dwarf who manages the site: they send them berserk.
